newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: PRESS DIGEST - Australian Sports News - July 22.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Australian Sports News - July 22.

text.p: (Compiled for Reuters by Media Monitors)
THE AUSTRALIAN

Australian Super League Brisbane prop Glenn Lazarus is not expected to play for the rest of the Australasian Super League season after suffering a broken leg. Lazarus will find out in the next 24 hours if the injury has done serious damage to his ankle whch he twisted during a World Cup Match. (Page 22).

Wicket-keeper for the Australian cricket side Ian Healy has described his loss of the position of Australia's Vice-Captain as a minor setback and personal blow. Healy said that personal goals should never get in the way of team goals and he is proud to be part of a good team. (Page 22).

Australian Football League Carlton player Ron DeIulio was suspended for four matches by the AFL tribunal last night for intentionally kicking an opposition team member, Essendon's Sam Kronja. DeIulio conceded that contact had been made but he neither inteded to injure or pursue Kronja with malice. (Page 22).

Champion Race Jockey Mick Dittman lost his appeal against a careless riding suspension yesterday which included a one-month penalty. Dittman said after the 90 minute hearing that he would be prepared to pursue the case further and take it to the Racing Apeals Authority to clear his name. (Page 22).
THE SYDNEY MORNING HERALD

Australian Football League Sydney Swans forward Tony Lockett has been fined a weeks wages - between A$10-A$15,000 - for wrestling West Coast Eagles opponent Fraser Gehrig during the first quarter confrontation on Saturday night. (Page 42).

Australian Rugby League props Mark Carroll and Terry Hermansson were cleared last night by the Australian Rugby League Judiciary for head butting. Manly prop Carroll could not believe he was in front of the Judiciary for such a charge and believes the game has become strict in its approach to discipline. (Page 42).

Euro League champions St Helens lost 28-12 in the World Cup Challenge Rugby League match played last night against Cronulla at Shark Park. The Lancashire side gave the Sharks, who were severely depleted of energy, a challenge before going down to the Austalian side. (Page 41)

Australian 100m record holder Damien Marsh has given up his bid to compete in the world athletic championships to be held in Athens nest month due to a failed attempt to reach qualifying standards in two sprints ran in Germany on Sunday. (Page 41).
THE AGE

Australian Football League Fremantle coach Gerard Neesham appears to be given a new contract by the Dockers board. Neesham comes out of his three year Fremantle contract at the end of the season. (Page B8).

Australian Football League Hawthorn player Chris Langford is expected to miss the match against Fremantle on Saturday due to a strained hamstring after the match with St. Kilda last Saturday. The Match was to be Langford's 300th commemorative game. (Page 8).

Australian Football League Sydney Swans players Shannon Grant and Jason Mooney all pleaded guilty to wrestling charges in front of the AFL tribunal last night. Also pleading guilty to charges was West Coast Eagles players Jason Ball and Ashley Blurton, all were fined according to their incomes. (Page B8)
THE HERALD SUN
Newspaper did not arrive today
THE DAILY TELEGRAPH

Sydney Rugby League Balmain centre Ian McCann will receive more than A$75, 000 after winning an out-of-court settlement against Mario Fenech. Fenech was reported to have injured McCann in a tackle which made McCann need 78 stitches. (Page 68).

Australian Rugby League team Canterbury won their World Cup Challenge match against Halifax yesterday 40-22. Canterbury winger Hazem El Mastri scored a hatrick of tries in the match which saw Halifax struggle to maintain their score. (Page 65)

Australian Super League rugby club Penrith are expected to spend around A$4 million to secure Craig Gower, Ryan Girdler and Matt Adamson. The three players have contacts which will expire at the end of the year and they are seeking other options. (Page 64.

Former Australian Rugby League Parramatta coach Jack Gibson believes the Eels will defeat Manly on Friday night. Gibson believes two players are the key to Parramatta's success in the past and will be a strong component to the Friday night game. Jim Dymoc and Jarrod McCracken are the players which Gibson believes strengthen the Parramatta side. (Page 60)
